TOOL_PINNING_DECISION.measured_skew: Clean-room finding: the governed rehearsal image scripts/baseline-rehearsal-local.ts REHEARSAL_IMAGE = public.ecr.aws/supabase/postgres:17.6.1.143, while the authorized staging target was measured LIVE (authority ADJUDICATIONS.L) at 17.6.1.155.
TOOL_PINNING_DECISION.measured_here: Both builds report PostgreSQL 17.6 (server_version_num 170006) and ship pg_dump/pg_restore/psql 17.6. The 17.6.1.155 image is present locally with image id sha256:3866d94d8426927e8db3f1c5d790752292bfbe27b5f1f46e199ae1b7d3c1710b (RepoDigest public.ecr.aws/supabase/postgres@sha256:3866d94d...). It declares NO Docker VOLUME (inspect .Mounts = []), so without an explicit mount PGDATA would live in the container layer.
TOOL_PINNING_DECISION.resolution: A SEPARATE recovery pin, not an edit of REHEARSAL_IMAGE: image reference public.ecr.aws/supabase/postgres:17.6.1.155, image id pinned by full sha256, PostgreSQL version 17.6 / server_version_num 170006 required EXACTLY for pg_dump, pg_restore, the source server, the substrate server and the artifact header. Any difference is a refusal, never a warning. The Supabase build suffix of the SOURCE is not visible over SQL and is therefore RECORDED as UNKNOWN_FROM_SQL, not asserted.
TOOL_PINNING_DECISION.why_exact_not_compatible: Logical dumps are portable across patch releases in principle, but the authority states 'tolerable in principle is not a measurement'. An exact pin fails closed on the first staging engine upgrade, which is the intended behaviour: the pin is then moved by a governed act, not absorbed silently.

CAPTURE_PRINCIPAL_CONTRACT.rule: The mechanism never invents a hosted privilege. It VERIFIES a principal it is given, by catalog predicates, before any capture byte is read.
predicates: rolsuper = false, rolcreaterole = false, rolcreatedb = false
no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER privilege on any in-scope relation
no CREATE privilege on any in-scope schema
rolbypassrls = true whenever any in-scope relation has FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY or RLS enabled (pg_dump runs with row_security = off and would otherwise fail or capture a filtered subset)
SELECT reachable on every in-scope relation
CAPTURE_PRINCIPAL_CONTRACT.hosted: Capture from a HOSTED_STAGING identity is REFUSED by this mechanism (RECOVERY_HOSTED_CAPTURE_NOT_AUTHORIZED). A future execution authority must supply the principal, run the SAME predicates against the authorized target, and lift that refusal by a governed change.
CAPTURE_PRINCIPAL_CONTRACT.local_tests: Disposable role recovery_capture_ro: LOGIN BYPASSRLS, member of pg_read_all_data, no per-object grant (so nothing about it is dumped).

MEASUREMENTS_THAT_SHAPED_THE_DESIGN: pg_dump 17.6 with -n public emits a 'SCHEMA - public' TOC entry, so pg_restore into a fresh database fails with 'schema public already exists'. The runner drops the EMPTY public schema of the freshly created restore database before pg_restore, so the artifact alone defines it.

That restore then exits 0 while schema public has a NULL ACL: the SECURITY DEFINER capability call fails with 'permission denied for schema public' — RR-CAP-7 reproduced on a synthetic fixture. Applying db/baseline/stella_g2_post_restore.sql repairs it. A restore judged by exit status would have PASSED.

pg_dump with -n does NOT emit CREATE EXTENSION for an extension living in an in-scope schema; the capture must name extensions explicitly (--extension), and the declared scope therefore carries an extension list.

The pinned image's pg_hba trusts 127.0.0.1 inside the container, so a disposable capture principal logs in AS ITSELF over the container loopback with no password; the container still has --network none.
docker rm -v removes ANONYMOUS volumes only; a NAMED volume survives it and needs docker volume rm. Both are verified absent afterwards.
